question: A man sold two TV sets for ₹7,200 each for neither gain nor loss. If he sold one TV set at a loss of 10%, then the other TV set is sold at a profit of :
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] **__Shortcut Trick__**

Two TV sets sold for ₹7,200 each.

No gain (or) no loss

If one TV sold at 10% loss.

If CP = 10, then Sp = 9

9 units = 7200

So, 10 units = 8000

Total SP = 7200 + 7200

⇒ Rs 14400

So, CP of the other TV = (14400 - 8000) = Rs 6400

Profit percentage = (800 / 6400) × 100 = 100 / 8 = 12.5%

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Two TV sets sold for ₹7,200 each.

No gain (or) no loss

If one TV sold at 10% loss.

**Concept used: **

SP = CP + Profit

Profit percentage = (Profit / CP) × 100 

**Calculation:**

CP of the TV = 7200 × 10/(10 - 1) = Rs. 8000

Total SP = 7200 + 7200 = Rs.14400

So, CP of the other TV = (14400 - 8000) = Rs. 6400

Profit = 7200 - 6400 = 800

The profit percentage = (800 / 6400) × 100

⇒ 100 / 8 = 12.5 %

**∴ The other TV set is sold at a profit of 121over2%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__** 

Profit is calculated on cost price and discount is calculated on marked price.

1b
